e-6112.knowledge_point: Determining the Units of a Derivative
e-6112.problem: A rocket is at a distance of $r(t)$ meters from the ground $t$ seconds after it is launched. What are the units of $\dfrac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}t}?$
e-6112.worked_solution:
We have that the height $r(t)$ is measured in meters and the time is measured in seconds. 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t): & \text{meters} \\ t: & \text{seconds}\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative $\dfrac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}t}$ measures a change in $r(t)$ over a change in $t.$ So, it represents a ratio of the units:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}: & \frac{\text{meters}}{\text{seconds}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\dfrac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}t}$ is measured in "meters per second".

e-270.knowledge_point: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function
e-270.problem:
Consider a spherical balloon with radius $r.$ As the balloon loses air, its volume $V$ decreases. What is the best interpretation of $V'(r)?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930198/assets/7f52288ca4670375413ecd5283bc2d15fbb332af311ead07986c1526d25e338a.png)
e-270.worked_solution:
The function $V(r)$ gives the volume of a sphere with radius $r.$ So

$$
V'(r) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}V}{\textrm{d}r} = \dfrac{\textrm{Change in }V}{\textrm{Change in }r}.
$$

Therefore, $V'(r)$ is the rate at which the volume changes as the radius changes.

e-271.knowledge_point: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function in a Given Context
e-271.problem: The function $B(s)$ models a school's budget, in dollars, given the average number of students $s$ in each grade. What is the best interpretation of $B'(30)=2\,000?$
e-271.worked_solution:
The function $B'(s)$ represents the rate at which the budget is changing at the moment when the school has an average of exactly $s$ students in each grade.

Therefore, $B'(30) = 2\,000$ means:

*When the school has an average of $30$ students in each grade, its budget is increasing at a rate of $2\,000$ dollars per student.*

e-273.problem:
On a particular day, the rate $E$ at which tourists enter a small country can be modeled as $E(t) = 50\cdot 3^{0.2t}$ tourists per hour, where $t$ is the time, in hours, after midnight. The rate at which tourists leave the country can be modeled as $L(t)=100\cdot 2^{0.2t}$ tourists per hour, where $t$ is also the time in hours after midnight.

What is the rate of change in the number of tourists in the country at $10\text{:}00\,\textrm{am}?$
e-273.worked_solution:
The rate of change of the number of tourists in the country at time $t$ is equal to the entry rate minus the exit rate at time $t,$ that is, 

$$
E(t)-L(t).
$$

Since $10\text{:}00\,\textrm{am}$ is ten hours after midnight, we have $t=10.$ Substituting $t=10,$ the rate of change in the number of tourists in the country at $10\text{:}00\,\textrm{am}$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}E(10)-L(10) & =50\cdot {3}^{0.2(10)}-100\cdot {2}^{0.2(10)} \\  & =450-400 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change in the number of tourists in the country at $10\text{:}00\,\textrm{am}$ is $50$ tourists per hour.

e-6113.knowledge_point: Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change
e-6113.problem:
Howard, the manager of a sci-fi convention, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of visitors to the convention, $t$ minutes after the convention has opened.

- $N(t)$ - the number of people inside the convention

- $E(t)$ - the rate at which people enter the convention

- $L(t)$ - the rate at which people leave the convention

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
e-6113.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of people inside the convention $t$ minutes after opening. Then,

$$
N'(t) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}N(t)}{\textrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\textrm{Change in }N}{\textrm{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, $N'(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of people inside the convention changes $t$ minutes after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of people inside the convention at time $t$ by finding the difference between the entry and exit rates at time $t.$ That is,

$$
N'(t) = E(t) - L(t).
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Consider a sphere such that its volume $V$ can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${r}^{′}(V)$ if $r$ is the length of the radius of the sphere?
after.worked_solution:
The function $r(V)$ gives the length of the radius of a sphere with volume $V.$ So,

$$
{r}^{′}(V)=\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}V}=\frac{\text{Change in }r}{\text{Change in }V}.
$$

Therefore, ${r}^{′}(V)$ is the rate at which the radius changes as the volume changes.

history.worked_solution:
The function $V(s)$ gives the volume of a cube with side $s.$ So,

$$
{V}^{′}(s)=\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}s}=\frac{\text{Change in }V}{\text{Change in }s}.
$$

Therefore, ${V}^{′}(s)$ is the rate at which the volume changes as each side changes.

Question 13
?

The function P(v) models the price of lemonade sold at a lemonade stand, in dollars, depending on the volume v sold the previous day, in liters. What is the best interpretation of the statement below?

The slope of the tangent line to the graph of P(v) at v=4 is equal to 0.5.

a
When the price of lemonade equals 50 cents, the amount sold increases at a rate of 4 liters per dollar
b
When the price of lemonade equals 50 cents, the amount sold decreases at a rate of 4 liters per dollar
c
When 4 liters of lemonade are sold the previous day, the price decreases at a rate of 50 cents per liter
d
When 4 liters of lemonade are sold the previous day, the price increases at a rate of 50 cents per liter
e
When 4 liters of lemonade were sold the previous day, the price of lemonade is equal to 50 cents.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The slope of the line tangent to the graph of P(v) at v=4 gives the derivative of P(v) at v=4. So, we have that P′(4)=0.5.

We can interpret the above statement as

When 4 liters of lemonade are sold the previous day, the price is increasing at a rate of 50 cents per liter.

before.html:
Question 15
?

The function S(t) gives the area, in squared centimeters, of a thin sheet of ice as it melts t minutes after observations start. What is the best interpretation of S′(5)=−7?

a
5 minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet decreases at a rate of 7 squared centimeters per minute
b
7 minutes after the observation began, the area of the sheet increases at a rate of 5 squared centimeters per minute
c
7 minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet is 5 squared centimeters
d
During the first 5 minutes of the observations, the area has constantly decreased at a rate of 7 squared centimeters per minute
e
5 minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet is 7 squared centimeters
Submit

decision.explanation: S′(5) = -7 means that at 5 minutes, the area is decreasing at an instantaneous rate of 7 squared centimeters per minute.

answers.correct_value: $5$ minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet decreases at a rate of $7$ squared centimeters per minute
answers.wrong_value: $5$ minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet is $7$ squared centimeters

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: The function $S(t)$ gives the area, in squared centimeters, of a thin sheet of ice as it melts $t$ minutes after observations start. What is the best interpretation of ${S}^{′}(5)=-7?$
after.worked_solution:
The function ${S}^{′}(t)$ represents the rate at which the area of the sheet is decreasing $t$ minutes after the beginning of the observation.

Therefore, since it is negative, ${S}^{′}(5)=-7$ means:

$\,$ *$5$ minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet decreases at a rate of $7$ squared centimeters per minute.*

Question 16
?

The decay rate M of muons in a beam traveling at high speed can be modeled by the function M(t)=2⋅e−2t, where t is the time, in microseconds, since observations started. What will be the decay rate of the muons after 0.5 microseconds? Round your answer to three decimal places.

a
0.899 muons per microsecond
b
0.566 muons per microsecond
c
0.311 muons per microsecond
d
0.346 muons per microsecond
e
0.736 muons per microsecond
Submit

decision.explanation: Substitute t = 0.5 into the given decay rate: M(0.5) = 2e^(-1) ≈ 0.735759, which rounds to 0.736 muons per microsecond.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem: The decay rate $M$ of muons in a beam traveling at high speed can be modeled by the function $M(t)=2\cdot {e}^{-2t},$ where $t$ is the time, in microseconds, since observations started. What will be the decay rate of the muons after $0.5$ microseconds? Round your answer to three decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
The function $M(t)$ models the decay rate for the particles $t$ microseconds since observations started.

Thus, the decay rate of the muons after $0.5$ microseconds is

$$
\begin{aligned}M(0.5) & =2\cdot {e}^{-2(0.5)} \\  & =2\cdot {e}^{-1} \\  & ≈0.736.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the decay rate of the particles is $0.736$ muons per microsecond.

The decay rate M of muons in a beam traveling at high speed can be modeled by the function M(t)=2⋅e−2t, where t is the time, in microseconds, since observations started. What will be the decay rate of the muons after 0.5 microseconds? Round your answer to three decimal places.

a
0.899 muons per microsecond
b
0.566 muons per microsecond
c
0.311 muons per microsecond
d
0.346 muons per microsecond
e
0.736 muons per microsecond

The function M(t) models the decay rate for the particles t microseconds since observations started.

Thus, the decay rate of the muons after 0.5 microseconds is M(0.5)=2⋅e−2(0.5)=2⋅e−1≈0.736.

Therefore, the decay rate of the particles is 0.736 muons per microsecond.

after.name: Question 17
after.problem: After charging the battery of a PC, the percentage of charge decreases at a rate of $c(t)=100\cdot {5}^{-0.2t}$ percent per hour, where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the battery had completed its charge. What will be the rate of decrease after $5$ hours?
after.worked_solution:
Since we want to determine the rate of decrease in the amount of charge after $5$ hours, we have $t=5.$

Thus, the rate of decrease of the amount of charge after $5$ hours will be

$$
\begin{aligned}c(5) & =100\cdot {5}^{-0.2(5)} \\  & =100\cdot {5}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{100}{5} \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of decrease will be $20$ percent per hour.

Jason, a biologist, is measuring the growth of bacteria in a Petri dish by recording the following two numbers for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

- $N(t)$ - the number of bacteria in the dish.

- $r(t)$ - the rate at which the number of bacteria in the dish is increasing.

What is the relationship between $N(t)$ and $r(t)?$

Question 21
?

Jason, a biologist, is measuring the growth of bacteria in a Petri dish by recording the following two numbers for different values of t, where t is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

  • N(t) - the number of bacteria in the dish.

  • r(t) - the rate at which the number of bacteria in the dish is increasing.

What is the relationship between N(t) and r(t)?

a
N′(t)=r(t)
b
N′(t)=−r(t)
c
 N(t)=−r′(t)
d
N(t)=r′(t)
e
 N(t)=r(t)
Submit

decision.explanation: N′(t) is the rate of change of the number of bacteria. Since r(t) is defined as that rate of increase, N′(t) = r(t).

after.name: Question 21
after.problem:
Jason, a biologist, is measuring the growth of bacteria in a Petri dish by recording the following two numbers for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

- $N(t)$ - the number of bacteria in the dish.

- $r(t)$ - the rate at which the number of bacteria in the dish is increasing.

What is the relationship between $N(t)$ and $r(t)?$
after.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of bacteria inside the dish after $t$ hours. Then,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}N(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }N}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${N}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of bacteria is increasing at time $t$, which is the same as $r(t).$ Therefore, the relationship between $N(t)$ and $r(t)$ is ${N}^{′}(t)=r(t).$

before.problem:
Liam, a farmer, is monitoring the construction of a fence by recording the following two numbers for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

after.name: Question 22
after.problem:
Liam, a farmer, is monitoring the construction of a fence by recording the following two numbers for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

- $P(t)$ - the number of panels in the fence.

- $r(t)$ - the rate at which the number of panels in the fence increases.

What is the relationship between $P(t)$ and $r(t)?$
after.worked_solution:
The function $P(t)$ gives the number of panels in the fence after $t$ hours. Then,

$$
{P}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}P(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }P}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${P}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of panels increases at time $t$, which is the same as $r(t).$ Therefore, the relationship between $P(t)$ and $r(t)$ is ${P}^{′}(t)=r(t).$

after.name: Question 23
after.problem:
Douglas, a pilot, is flying a plane. The plane's control systems record two measurements for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in minutes, since take off. The two measurements are:

- $A(t)$ - the altitude (height) of the plane

- $r(t)$ the rate at which the altitude is increasing

What is the relationship between $A(t)$ and $r(t)?$
after.worked_solution:
The function $A(t)$ gives the altitude of the plane after $t$ hours. Then,

$$
{A}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}A(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }A}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${A}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the altitude is increasing at time $t$, which is the same as $r(t).$ Therefore, the relationship between $A(t)$ and $r(t)$ is ${A}^{′}(t)=r(t).$

before.html:
Question 24
?

Oliver, the owner of a platform for chess players, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of users of the platform t days after it was launched.

  • N(t) - the number of users with an account

  • O(t) - the rate at which new users open an account

  • C(t) - the rate at which users cancel their account

What is the relationship between the three functions above?

a
N(t)=−O(t)−C(t)
b
N′(t)=O(t)+C(t)
c
N(t)=O(t)−C(t)
d
N′(t)=O(t)−C(t)
e
N(t)=O(t)+C(t)
Submit

decision.explanation: The rate of change of the number of accounts equals the rate of new accounts minus the rate of cancellations: N′(t) = O(t) − C(t).

after.name: Question 24
after.problem:
Oliver, the owner of a platform for chess players, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of users of the platform $t$ days after it was launched.

- $N(t)$ - the number of users with an account

- $O(t)$ - the rate at which new users open an account

- $C(t)$ - the rate at which users cancel their account

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
after.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of users $t$ days after the platform is set up. Then,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}N(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }N}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${N}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of users with an account changes $t$ days after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of users at time $t$ by finding the difference between the open and cancel rates at time $t.$ That is,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=O(t)-C(t).
$$

after.html:
Question 24
?

Oliver, the owner of a platform for chess players, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of users of the platform t days after it was launched.

  • N(t) - the number of users with an account

  • O(t) - the rate at which new users open an account

  • C(t) - the rate at which users cancel their account

What is the relationship between the three functions above?

a
N(t)=−O(t)−C(t)
b
N′(t)=O(t)+C(t)
c
N(t)=O(t)−C(t)
d
N′(t)=O(t)−C(t)
e
N(t)=O(t)+C(t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function N(t) gives the number of users t days after the platform is set up. Then, N′(t)=dN(t)dt=Change in NChange in t. Thus, N′(t) gives the rate at which the number of users with an account changes t days after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of users at time t by finding the difference between the open and cancel rates at time t. That is, N′(t)=O(t)−C(t).

content.knowledge_point: Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change
content.problem:
Oliver, the owner of a platform for chess players, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of users of the platform $t$ days after it was launched.

- $N(t)$ - the number of users with an account

- $O(t)$ - the rate at which new users open an account

- $C(t)$ - the rate at which users cancel their account

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
content.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of users $t$ days after the platform is set up. Then,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}N(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }N}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${N}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of users with an account changes $t$ days after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of users at time $t$ by finding the difference between the open and cancel rates at time $t.$ That is,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=O(t)-C(t).
$$

Question 25

To measure the number of children visiting a playground, Noah uses the following three functions that model the hourly number of visitors to the playground t hours after the playground is opened to the public.

  • N(t) - the number of children inside the playground

  • E(t) - the rate at which children enter the playground

  • L(t) - the rate at which children leave the playground

What is the relationship between the functions above?

a
N(t)=E(t)+L(t)
b
N(t)=E(t)−L(t)
c
N′(t)=E(t)⋅L(t)
d
N′(t)=E(t)+L(t)
e
N′(t)=E(t)−L(t)
Submit

decision.explanation: The number of children changes at the entry rate minus the exit rate, so N′(t) = E(t) − L(t).

after.name: Question 25
after.problem:
To measure the number of children visiting a playground, Noah uses the following three functions that model the hourly number of visitors to the playground $t$ hours after the playground is opened to the public.

- $N(t)$ - the number of children inside the playground

- $E(t)$ - the rate at which children enter the playground

- $L(t)$ - the rate at which children leave the playground

What is the relationship between the functions above?
after.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of children inside the park $t$ minutes after opening. Then,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}N(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }N}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${N}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of children inside the playground changes $t$ hours after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of children inside the playground at time $t$ by finding the difference between the entry and exit rates at time $t.$ That is,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=E(t)-L(t).
$$

Question 25
?

To measure the number of children visiting a playground, Noah uses the following three functions that model the hourly number of visitors to the playground t hours after the playground is opened to the public.

  • N(t) - the number of children inside the playground

  • E(t) - the rate at which children enter the playground

  • L(t) - the rate at which children leave the playground

What is the relationship between the functions above?

a
N(t)=E(t)+L(t)
b
N(t)=E(t)−L(t)
c
N′(t)=E(t)⋅L(t)
d
N′(t)=E(t)+L(t)
e
N′(t)=E(t)−L(t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function N(t) gives the number of children inside the park t minutes after opening. Then, N′(t)=dN(t)dt=Change in NChange in t. Thus, N′(t) gives the rate at which the number of children inside the playground changes t hours after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of children inside the playground at time t by finding the difference between the entry and exit rates at time t. That is, N′(t)=E(t)−L(t).

content.knowledge_point: Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change
content.problem:
To measure the number of children visiting a playground, Noah uses the following three functions that model the hourly number of visitors to the playground $t$ hours after the playground is opened to the public.

- $N(t)$ - the number of children inside the playground

- $E(t)$ - the rate at which children enter the playground

- $L(t)$ - the rate at which children leave the playground

What is the relationship between the functions above?
content.worked_solution:
The function $N(t)$ gives the number of children inside the park $t$ minutes after opening. Then,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}N(t)}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{Change in }N}{\text{Change in }t}.
$$

Thus, ${N}^{′}(t)$ gives the rate at which the number of children inside the playground changes $t$ hours after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of children inside the playground at time $t$ by finding the difference between the entry and exit rates at time $t.$ That is,

$$
{N}^{′}(t)=E(t)-L(t).
$$
